I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything too fancy. On my 10.9 mu, I will still keep the land split the way that feels safest for my family: most of it in wheat-maize rotation, and a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize are steady for us, and cotton gives another income road if grain price is not good. I only finished primary school, so I mostly farm by what I’ve seen on my own land and what the neighbors do. Last year the wheat-maize land still gave decent return with moderate fertilizer and 2 to 3 irrigations, so this year I won’t cut too much. Fertilizer is expensive, but if I save too much on it and the crop turns weak, that loss is bigger. At the same time, some people in the family work outside, so I cannot make a plan that needs too much careful labor every day. Cotton I keep on a smaller area because it needs more watching and more picking labor.

For wheat, I’ll put about 7 mu into the wheat-maize rotation. I’ll sow in early October with the local wheat seed most people use, not the expensive special kind. I’ll put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once at jointing if the stand looks good enough to deserve it. I have well water, so I’ll irrigate around wintering, jointing, and filling if the spring stays dry. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll rush to plant summer maize right away on the same 7 mu because the window is short. I’ll use hybrid maize seed, do simpler field prep, put fertilizer once at sowing and once around knee-high stage, and give one or two irrigations if rain is short. For cotton, I’ll keep 3.9 mu. Cotton can make money, but it ties up labor, so I won’t expand it. I’ll use ordinary improved seed, feed it in two doses, water it a couple of times, and spray only when I really see insects or too many weeds.
